item.title: Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls
item.description:
Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls

Apple is updating Siri to become more agentic, adding fine‑grained control over its own apps and integration with third‑party services.

🔍 Overview

  • Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap.
  • Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, but the company acknowledges it is not keeping pace with rivals.
  • Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic and to enable ongoing tasks rather than single‑step commands.

⚙️ Upcoming Features

  • Fine‑grained control of first‑party apps – Siri will be able to rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Expected with iOS 27.3.
  • Third‑party app integration – Siri will place orders through Grubhub, book reservations through OpenTable, and similar actions. Expected in the Spring following iOS 27.3.

📅 Timeline

Feature Expected Release
First‑party app control (Photos, Safari) iOS 27.3
Third‑party app integration (Grubhub, OpenTable) Spring after iOS 27.3

💡 Why it matters

  • Competitors such as OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and Grok can keep track of goals and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every step.
  • Apple aims to give Siri similar agentic capabilities, allowing it to perform ongoing tasks and manage objectives, a direction the company may reach as early as next year.

#Apple #Siri #AIagents #VoiceAssistants

Source: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic

item.title: Evaluation of LLM Decision Alignment in Vehicle Voice Assistants
item.description:
Evaluation of LLM Decision Alignment in Vehicle Voice Assistants

Researchers have evaluated the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into vehicle voice assistants using a new benchmark to test decision-making safety.

🔍 Overview

Before executing a command, vehicle voice assistants must decide between seven possible actions:

  • Execute
  • Refuse
  • Clarify
  • Require confirmation
  • Defer to manual control
  • Trigger an emergency response
  • Make no tool call

⚙️ Key details

The study utilized a 202-scenario benchmark with Reference Decisions to evaluate two local open-weight models and three API-based LLMs.

Model Decision Alignment
Llama 3.2 3B 40.1%
Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 89.1%

Key findings include:

  • API-based models scored between 83.2% and 89.1%, showing no statistically significant differences among them.
  • Even top-performing models produced two to three False Executes across 161 non-execution scenarios.
  • Persistent errors remain in manual-control and confirmation decisions.
  • A controlled Llama 3.2 3B ablation using a structured authorization policy increased alignment to 40.1%, compared to 28.2-29.2% under generic-safety and schema-only baselines, though False Executes were not eliminated.

💡 Why it matters

Because structured LLM decisions are insufficient as a standalone safety mechanism, deployment requires an independent enforcement layer to verify vehicle-state constraints and tool permissions before any vehicle function is invoked.

#LLM #AutomotiveAI #AISafety #VoiceAssistants

Source: From Intent to Action: Benchmarking LLM Safety in Vehicle Voice Command Authorization Source: Dictionary-Constrained Grapheme-to-Phoneme for Unsegmented Languages from LLM-Annotated Data
